tagline: USSF reusable robotic spaceplane — multi-year classified orbital missions, the only US spaceplane operational after the Shuttle's retirement
description: Robotic mini-spaceplane (8.9 m long, ~5 t) built by Boeing Phantom Works for the USAF, transferred to the USSF in 2019. Launches vertically (Atlas V 501 originally; SpaceX Falcon 9 from OTV-5; Falcon Heavy from OTV-7) and lands horizontally on Kennedy's former Shuttle runway. Most payloads and orbital parameters are classified — known mission durations stretch from 224 days (OTV-1, 2010) to a record 908 days (OTV-6, 2020-2022). Declassified experiments include Hall-effect thruster tech demo, an AFRL radio-frequency communication test, and a 1 W solar-power-to-microwave-beaming experiment (PRAM, OTV-6). As of 2026 has flown seven missions.
best_known_for: USSF reusable robotic spaceplane — classified multi-year orbital missions, post-Shuttle US spaceplane
